data.q: In CRAG, who decides if retrieved chunks are relevant?
data.a: A grader model, run before generation. Paper: a small fine-tuned T5 gives each doc a score; two cutoffs turn scores into correct / ambiguous / incorrect. Our lab: the LLM grades all chunks in one batched call. Cheaper option: cross-encoder score with a cutoff. The grader makes mistakes too, so its precision matters most.

data.b:
Problem: naive RAG trusts whatever retrieval returns.
So: an LLM grader checks each chunk first.
  • some relevant -> answer from those only
  • none -> rewrite query, hybrid search, grade again (max 2)
  • still none -> "Not in the sources"
Evidence: 22 -> 23/25 correct, but 2.2 LLM calls/q vs 1.0.

data.t: Value depends on how often retrieval fails
data.b:
Problem: retriever ranks by similarity, not 'answers it?'.
So: CRAG helps when similarity misleads:
  • Duplicates crowd out the answer chunk
  • Old pages score like new ones
  • User wording far from doc wording (rewrite fixes)
Evidence: clean docs: naive 22/25, CRAG 23/25 (the EXPIRE_MAKER rewrite), 2.2x calls.

data.q: Top-k is filled with relevant near-duplicates. Does CRAG fetch the other useful chunks?
data.a: No. The grader checks each chunk alone, so all copies pass and no retry starts. It does not check coverage or diversity. Fix before grading: dedupe, MMR, or fetch more then rerank. Or grade the whole set: 'is this enough to answer?'

data.q: How do you remove duplicate chunks in RAG?
data.a:
1. Exact: normalize + hash
  2. Near, by text: MinHash / SimHash
  3. Near, by meaning: embedding cosine above a tuned threshold
Clean at index time first (1+2, keep newest). At query time, fetch more, then MMR. Risk: merging chunks that differ in one number.

data.q: What is MMR and why use it in retrieval?
data.a:
Problem: top-k by similarity can return k copies.
So: pick chunks one by one: λ*sim(query) - (1-λ)*max sim(picked). A chunk like one already picked loses points.
λ sets relevance vs variety. Nothing is deleted from the index, unlike MinHash/SimHash dedupe.

data.q: Dedupe at index time or query time?
data.a:
Problem: copies fill top-k before query-time dedupe can run, and they skew BM25.
So: delete exact copies at index time. Tag near copies with a group id, then keep one per group at query time. Use MMR for the rest.
Query-time only = must over-fetch, with no safe size.
